legend: There is a hidden positive integer k%%ZSMJ0%% that has exactly n%%ZSMJ1%% divisors. These divisors were put into an array a%%ZSMJ2%% which was then shuffled into a hidden order.

You can ask the interactor questions of the form ? i j, and you will receive the position of gcd(ai,aj)%%ZSMJ3%% in a%%ZSMJ4%%. Note that since a%%ZSMJ5%% contains all divisors of k%%ZSMJ6%%, this value is guaranteed to exist and be unique.
Using at most 3n%%ZSMJ7%% queries, determine which indices of a%%ZSMJ8%% contain prime numbers.
input: The input consists of one line containing an integer n%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤n≤104%%ZSMJ10%%) — the number of divisors of k%%ZSMJ11%%.
Note that we make no guarantees about the magnitude of k%%ZSMJ12%%.
After reading in n%%ZSMJ13%%, you can make up to 3n%%ZSMJ14%% queries.
For each query, print a line of the form ? i j (1≤i,j≤n%%ZSMJ15%%).
After printing the query, you can then read in an integer x%%ZSMJ16%%, where ax=gcd(ai,aj)%%ZSMJ17%%.

Once you have determined which indices contain prime numbers, print a single line ! m p_1 p_2 ... p_m (0≤m≤n%%ZSMJ18%%, 1≤pi≤n%%ZSMJ19%%, where m%%ZSMJ20%% is the number of prime factors and p1%%ZSMJ21%% through pm%%ZSMJ22%% are their positions in a%%ZSMJ23%%. This is not counted towards your total of 3n%%ZSMJ24%% queries.
After printing a query do not forget to output the end of line and flush the output. Otherwise, you will get Idleness limit exceeded. To do this, use:
see the documentation for other languages.
The interactor is non-adaptive. This means that the array a%%ZSMJ25%% is fixed at the start of the interaction, and does not change after the queries.
note: In the first test, after the first query, we know that gcd(a2,a4)=a1%%ZSMJ26%%. It can be shown that since n=4%%ZSMJ27%%, this query result implies that a2%%ZSMJ28%% and a4%%ZSMJ29%% are the prime factors of k%%ZSMJ30%%.

In the second test n=1%%ZSMJ31%%, and therefore k=1%%ZSMJ32%%, because 1%%ZSMJ33%% is the only positive integer with only one divisor. Since 1%%ZSMJ34%% has no prime factors, we can simply output ! 0 without making any queries.
